endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: W hen AI is used in a manner which impacts access to care or impacts medical decision making at the point of care, that use of AI should be disclosed and documented to both physicians and/or patients in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.

endorsements.title: Beyond the Algorithm: A Perspective on Tackling Bias and Cultural Sensitivity in AI-Guided Aesthetic Standards for Cosmetic Surgery in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) Region
endorsements.quote: Informed consent protocols must be culturally adapted to ensure patients understand AI\u2019s role in their assessment, including potential cultural biases and limitations.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether culturally adapted AI disclosures improve patient understanding or trust, and no study documents how often current disclosures fail culturally diverse patients. The recommendation rests on one professional guidance document and one regional commentary.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard. The two endorsements are a guidance statement and a commentary focused on cosmetic surgery in the Middle East and North Africa. Neither reports data, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence, and the size of any benefit remains unknown.

The recommendation targets culturally and linguistically diverse patients, yet no supplied study measured disclosure comprehension in any population. Health systems therefore lack evidence on which adaptations, such as translation, plain-language rewriting, or community review, change understanding for the groups most likely to be misserved.

commentary.research_gap: Trials or controlled comparisons are needed that test culturally and linguistically adapted AI disclosures against standard disclosures, measuring patient comprehension, trust, and decisions about care. Descriptive studies are also needed to establish how often current AI disclosures are misunderstood across cultural and language groups.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence exists for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Systems serving these groups would be adopting the practice on the strength of expert opinion alone and may wish to evaluate their own disclosures locally.
